                                                      AGENDA
1. Call to Order

   A. Pledge of Allegiance

   B. Council Clerk Reads the Call of the Meeting and Mayor declares call a legal call and meeting a legal meeting

2. Public Hearings -- Proposed Bond Ordinances, appropriating $38,000,000 for Board of Education
   Capital Improvement Plan and $30,426,000 for construction of new downtown parking arcade

   A. Public Hearings on Proposed Bond Ordinances

       Mayor requests Council Clerk to read legal notices for proposed bond ordinance appropriations
       and the Certificate of the Director of Finance & Revenue Services

       (1) An ordinance appropriating $30,426,000 for Phase I of the Middletown Public Schools Districtwide
           Infrastructure Project, and authorizing the issue of $30,426,000 bonds of the City to meet said
           appropriation, and, pending the issuance thereof, that making of temporary borrowings for such
           purpose.
       (2) An ordinance appropriating $38,000,000 for the Downtown area parking facility project, and authorizing
           the issue of $38,000,000 bonds of the City to meet said appropriation, and, pending the issue thereof,
           the making of temporary borrowings for such purpose.
AUGUST 20, 2026                       COMMON COUNCIL – SPECIAL MEETING                                            Page 2


     B. Public Hearing on All Other Agenda Items

     C. Public Hearing Closes

3. Resolutions, Ordinances, etc.

   A. Bond Ordinance Appropriations

      i.       Approving Bond Ordinance Appropriation – Board of Education: an ordinance appropriating
               $30,426,000 for Phase I of the Middletown Public Schools Districtwide Infrastructure Project, and
               authorizing the issue of $30,426,000 bonds of the City to meet said appropriation, and, pending the
               issuance thereof, the making of temporary borrowings for such purpose.

     ii.       Approving Bond Ordinance Appropriation – Economic & Community Development: an ordinance
               appropriating $38,000,000 for the Downtown area parking facility project, and authorizing the issue of
               $38,000,000 bonds of the City to meet said appropriation, and, pending the issuance thereof, the
               making of temporary borrowings for such purpose.

   B. Approving Bond Ordinance for Referendum – Board of Education :

           Approving that the ordinance entitled AN ORDINANCE APPROPRIATING $30,426,000 FOR PHASE I OF
           THE MIDDLETOWN PUBLIC SCHOOLS DISTRICTWIDE INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT AND
           AUTHORIZING THE ISSUE OF $30,426,000 BONDS OF THE CITY TO MEET SAID APPROPRIATION
           AND PENDING THE ISSUANCE THEREOF THE MAKING OF TEMPORARY BORROWINGS FOR SUCH
           PURPOSE, as adopted by this meeting of the Common Council, be submitted to a referendum vote of the
           electors of the City for approval or disapproval in conjunction with the general election on November 3,
           2026 and that the warning of said referendum state the question to be voted upon and the ballot label with
           respect thereto as follows:

           Question 1:

           “Shall the ordinance entitled AN ORDINANCE APPROPRIATING $30,426,000 FOR PHASE I OF THE
           MIDDLETOWN PUBLIC SCHOOLS DISTRICTWIDE INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT AND
           AUTHORIZING THE ISSUE OF $30,426,000 BONDS OF THE CITY TO MEET SAID APPROPRIATION
           AND PENDING THE ISSUANCE THEREOF THE MAKING OF TEMPORARY BORROWINGS FOR SUCH
           PURPOS, as adopted by the Common Council on August 20, 2026, be approved? YES ____ NO_____”

           The ballot label for said question shall read as follows:

           “Shall the $30,426,000 appropriation and bond authorization for Phase I of the Middletown Public Schools
           Districtwide Infrastructure Project be approved? YES ___ NO ____”

           The voting will be by paper/electronic ballot. Those desiring to vote for the question shall fill in the box in
           front of the question on the ballot at “YES.” Those desiring to vote against the question shall fill in the box
           in front of the question on the ballot at “NO.” Absentee ballots will be made available in accordance with
           the law.

           The referendum shall be warned, noticed, conducted, canvassed, determined, and certified in accordance
           with applicable provisions of the Connecticut General Statutes, including Title 9 and the provisions
           governing early in-person voting to the extent applicable.

           The warning of said referendum shall also state that the full text of the aforesaid ordinance and question
           are on file open to public inspection in the office of the City and Town Clerk, that the vote on the aforesaid
           bond ordinance is taken pursuant to Chapter IX, Section 2 of the City Charter and Chapters 90 and 152 of
           the Connecticut General Statutes, as amended, and that absentee ballots will be made available in
AUGUST 20, 2026                   COMMON COUNCIL – SPECIAL MEETING                                            Page 3


       accordance with the law.

       The City and Town Clerk is hereby authorized and directed to prepare and print pursuant to section 9-369b
       of the Connecticut General Statutes (i) explanatory text for the foregoing question and (ii) materials
       concerning such question in addition to the explanatory text

   C. Approving Bond Ordinance for Referendum – Economic & Community Development:

       Approving that the ordinance entitled AN ORDINANCE APPROPRIATING $38,000,000 FOR THE
       DOWNTOWN AREA PARKING FACILITY PROJECT AND AUTHORIZING THE ISSUE OF $38,000,000
       BONDS OF THE CITY TO MEET SAID APPROPRIATION AND PENDING THE ISSUANCE THEREOF
       THE MAKING OF TEMPORARY BORROWINGS FOR SUCH PURPOSE, as adopted by this meeting of
       the Common Council, be submitted to a referendum vote of the electors of the City for approval or
       disapproval in conjunction with the general election on November 3, 2026 and that the warning of said
       referendum state the question to be voted upon and the ballot label with respect thereto as follows:

       Question 2:

       “Shall the ordinance entitled AN ORDINANCE APPROPRIATING $38,000,000 FOR THE DOWNTOWN
       AREA PARKING FACILITY PROJECT AND AUTHORIZING THE ISSUE OF $38,000,000 BONDS OF THE
       CITY TO MEET SAID APPROPRIATION AND PENDING THE ISSUANCE THEREOF THE MAKING OF
       TEMPORARY BORROWINGS FOR SUCH PURPOSE, as adopted by the Common Council on August 20,
       2026, be approved? YES ____ NO_____”

       The ballot label for said question shall read as follows:

       “Shall the $38,000,000 appropriation and bond authorization for the Downtown Area Parking Facility Project
       be approved? YES ___ NO ____”

       The voting will be by paper/electronic ballot. Those desiring to vote for the question shall fill in the box in
       front of the question on the ballot at “YES.” Those desiring to vote against the question shall fill in the box
       in front of the question on the ballot at “NO.” Absentee ballots will be made available in accordance with
       the law.

       The referendum shall be warned, noticed, conducted, canvassed, determined, and certified in accordance
       with applicable provisions of the Connecticut General Statutes, including Title 9 and the provisions
       governing early in-person voting to the extent applicable.

       The warning of said referendum shall also state that the full text of the aforesaid ordinance and question
       are on file open to public inspection in the office of the City and Town Clerk, that the vote on the aforesaid
       bond ordinance is taken pursuant to Chapter IX, Section 2 of the City Charter and Chapters 90 and 152 of
       the Connecticut General Statutes, as amended, and that absentee ballots will be made available in
       accordance with the law.

       The City and Town Clerk is hereby authorized and directed to prepare and print pursuant to section 9-
       369b of the Connecticut General Statutes (i) explanatory text for the foregoing question and (ii) materials
       concerning such question in addition to the explanatory text.

   D. Approving that Zion First Baptist Church’s sponsored special event, Soul on the Green, will be held on
      Saturday, August 29, 2026, from 1:00 PM to 4:00 PM on Middletown Green, providing the community with
      a free, end-of summer concert with rhythm, blues, and timeless jazz; that the Showmobile shall be made
      available for this event and any and all fees, including personnel fees for the Showmobile, shall be waived;
      and that the City of Middletown shall expend no more than $1,000 for personnel fees for said event without
      further Councilmanic approval.
AUGUST 20, 2026                       COMMON COUNCIL – SPECIAL MEETING                    Page 4




4. Mayor’s Appointments

5.   Adjournment
